{{Short description|Chinese-American physicist (1952–2017)}}
'''Po-Zen Wong''' (6 November 1952 – 16 October 2017) was a Chinese-American physicist.

Wong was born in Shanghai on 6 November 1952. He lived in Hong Kong from the age of four until earning his Bachelor of Science in physics from the [[Chinese University of Hong Kong]]. Wong subsequently moved to the United States, where he completed a PhD at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1981. After working for [[Schlumberger Doll Research]], Wong taught at the [[University of Massachusetts at Amherst]] from 1988 to August 2008.<ref name="physnewsletter"/><ref name="obit"/> Wong was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2000, "[f]or studies of disordered magnetic systems, porous media, and random interfaces."<ref name="apsfa">{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=Po-zen%20Wong&af=true |access-date=15 July 2026 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref>

In retirement, and inspired by his father Nan-Ping Wong, Po-Zen Wong became a collector of Chinese art.<ref name="physnewsletter">{{cite news |title=People: Po-Zen Wong |url=https://scholarworks.umass.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/d525365a-f9b3-4293-bea2-f7e7cf1470a1/content |access-date=15 July 2026 |publisher=University of Massachusetts Amherst Department of Physics |date=Spring 2008}}</ref><ref name="obit">{{cite news |title=Po-zen Wong |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/gazettenet/name/po-zen-wong-obituary?id=11453019 |access-date=15 July 2026 |work=Daily Hampshire Gazette |date=21 October 2017}}</ref> Wong died at the age of 64 on 16 October 2017.<ref name="obit"/>
